## `src/mcp/prompts.rs`

### src/mcp/prompts.rs:330

````text
The published tool list is capability-filtered, so this checks the
prompts that are actually published against the tools that are
actually available.
````

### src/mcp/prompts.rs:347

````text
Even a prompt that is hidden under the default capabilities may not
name a tool that does not exist at all.
````

### src/mcp/prompts.rs:403

````text
`spectre-failure-triage` names `skill_exec`, which needs the Admin
capability — the default capability set does not have it.
````

### src/mcp/prompts.rs:437

````text
An explicit null is as good as missing.
````

## `src/mcp/resources.rs`

### src/mcp/resources.rs:177

````text
Symlinked skill directories are refused with the same rule the
read path applies: a directory that resolves outside the skills
root must not be published, because reading it would fail
anyway — listing it would advertise a resource that cannot be
read and leak its frontmatter description.
````

### src/mcp/resources.rs:188

````text
Resolve the skill file through the read path so a symlinked
SKILL.md is skipped here exactly as it is refused on read.
````

### src/mcp/resources.rs:205

````text
Stable, deterministic order — clients list resources in this order.
````

### src/mcp/resources.rs:314

````text
A blank line is part of the block scalar — it does not end it.
````

### src/mcp/resources.rs:323

````text
The first non-empty, non-indented line ends the block.
````

### src/mcp/resources.rs:347

````text
Blank lines inside the block are structural, not content: they are
dropped from the one-line description.
````

### src/mcp/resources.rs:578

````text
A symlink inside the root must not become a read primitive.
````

### src/mcp/resources.rs:588

````text
`..` never even reaches the filesystem.
````

## `src/mcp/server.rs`

### src/mcp/server.rs:10

````text
A set-but-invalid VB_SKILLS_DIR is a configuration error: serving a
different skills root than the operator asked for is worse than
refusing to start.
````

### src/mcp/server.rs:17

````text
Resolve the active target via the canonical selection path so the MCP
server inherits the same target identity as any other CLI invocation —
NOT a bare env-only Config that ignores targets.yaml.
````

### src/mcp/server.rs:88

````text
Replicate the exact selection chain mcp::server::run() uses.
````

### src/mcp/server.rs:133

````text
resolve_selection itself validates that active_target exists in
the targets map — it fails early rather than returning a
Selection that resolve_from_selection would later reject.
````
